story.head: Gauthier lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Never count the Ducks out. Philip Tomasino scored his first goal for Ottawa early in the first to open the scoring, and Claude Giroux made it 2-0 just over a minute later. Michael Amadio stretched the lead to 3-0 late in the period, and that was all they would get. Cutter Gauthier and Judd Caulfield scored just under two minutes apart early in the second to cut Ottawa’s lead to 3-2. Caulfield scored again on the power play late in the period to tie it 3-3. Gauthier scored again on the power play early in the third to put the Ducks ahead for the first time. Gauthier completed his hat trick on the power play 36 seconds later to make it 5-3. Roger McQueen pushed the lead to 6-3 on the power play with less than five minutes left. Two players had three-point nights: Leo Carlsson with three assists, and Caulfield with two goals and an assist.

The Ducks outshot the Senators 33-22, but the Senators’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. It was Laurent Brossoit’s first NHL win since Apr 18, 2024. Jonas Johansson allowed six goals on 33 shots for the Senators.

The power plays decided it: Caulfield, Gauthier and McQueen all scored on the power play as the Ducks turned a three-goal hole into the lead, and the Senators went 0-for-3 on theirs. Dylan Cozens was thrown out with a five-minute major for interference and a game misconduct midway through the third. The Ducks moved to 6-7-1 and climbed to fifth in the Pacific, while the Sens dropped to 9-6-1, third in the Atlantic.
